subject: Greta Gerwig
hook: This pink paint supposedly ran out because of one movie.
twist: The shortage was real but local to one supplier; the 'world ran out of pink' line was an offhand remark Greenwood later walked back.
mood: Glossy pastel 1960s toy-catalogue gouache in bubblegum pink and mint on cream card, soft flat shapes, gentle halftone grain. Music: bright light-pop with pizzicato strings, celesta and soft marimba, about 108 bpm, playful and tongue-in-cheek.
narration: This pink paint supposedly ran out because of one movie. In twenty twenty-two, designers built Barbieland in England for Greta Gerwig. She wanted the pinks very bright, and everything almost too much. Designer Sarah Greenwood needed a fluorescent pink from Rosco, a scenic paint supplier. Greenwood says they asked for two hundred liters of pure pigment. Rosco, already short after pandemic delays, told the Los Angeles Times the production cleaned them out. Greenwood told Architectural Digest the world ran out of pink. Headlines ran with it. Later, she called it an offhand remark. Pink paint turned up in backyard workshops. The shortage was real. It just belonged to one company, not the planet. Too much pink, or just enough?

captions.instagram_caption:
Did one movie really use up the world's pink paint? 🎀

Building Barbieland in 2022, production designer Sarah Greenwood needed a fluorescent pink from the scenic paint maker Rosco. Her team says they asked for two hundred liters of pure pigment.

Rosco, still recovering from pandemic delays and a Texas freeze, said the production cleaned them out. Greenwood told Architectural Digest that the world ran out of pink.

Later she called that an offhand remark and said the world never ran out. The shortage was real, but it belonged to one company.
